primary_source.headline: Three months on, no aid for pregnant women
primary_source.content: Tumakuru: Karnataka Mining Environment Restoration Corporation (KMERC) had planned to provide financial assistance to pregnant women in mining-affected areas to reduce maternal mortality. However, even three months after the details of the beneficiaries were submitted, the money has not been credited to their accounts.The scheme was launched in March 2025. In the first phase, 3,200 pregnant women from the mining-affected Chikkanayakanahalli, Gubbi and Tiptur taluks in the district were identified. Health Department officials had submitted the required details to the corporation. An amount of Rs 11.67 crore per year has been approved for the district. However, no money has so far been credited to the accounts of the pregnant women.People living in mining-affected areas are also facing health problems. Mining dust has affected not only the environment but also the respiratory health of residents. KMER-C has taken up various measures for environmental restoration. The new scheme was introduced as part of efforts to protect public health, but it has faced hurdles right from the beginning.WHO to launch new guidelines for pregnant women with NCDsUnder the scheme, Rs 8,850 will be provided for the first delivery. For the second delivery, Rs 8,850 will be given if the child is a girl and Rs 14,850 if it is a boy. The amount will reportedly be released by KMER-C in four instalments. So far, however, not a single beneficiary has received the money.Along with the financial assistance, it has also been decided to provide pregnant women with a nutritional kit after they complete six months of pregnancy. The kit will contain iron syrup, dates, a towel, ghee, medicines and other nutritious food items. The cost of each kit is estimated at Rs 2,250.“Three months ago, we submitted a report to the government and sent the details of around 3,000 pregnant women. The three taluks are expected to have 7,000 to 8,000 beneficiaries annually,” a Health Department official said.AIIMS study warns of air pollution impact on pregnant womenMaternal mortality declines Maternal and infant mortality in the district has been declining year by year. In 2021–22 37 mothers and 315 infants died. In 2025–26 the number fell to 11 maternal deaths and 256 infant deaths. Obstetricians and gynaecologists have been appointed at all taluk hospitals which has helped improve healthcare for pregnant women. Child-care units are functioning at the district hospital as well as hospitals in Tiptur Sira and Madhugiri. Pregnant women are being provided nutritious food and advised to take proper care of their health. These measures have played a major role in reducing maternal and infant mortality.

brief_bullets: Three months after local health authorities submitted beneficiary details, the Karnataka Mining Environment Restoration Corporation has failed to disburse financial assistance to pregnant women in mining-affected regions of Tumakuru district. primary_source.headline: IAEA board passes resolution reporting Iran to UN Security Council
primary_source.content: Vienna: The UN nuclear watchdog's 35-nation board of governors has passed a resolution reporting Iran to the UN Security Council for the first time in 20 years for breaching its non-proliferation obligations, diplomats said on Wednesday.The resolution follows up on a previous one passed on June 12 last year — the day before Israel started bombing Iran's nuclear facilities, soon followed by the United States — that found Iran in "non-compliance" with those obligations. Reporting it to the council for that breach required another resolution.Iran threatens US with new 'economic warfare' and missiles as Houthis attack Saudi ArabiaWhile the Security Council is unlikely to take concrete action against Iran since its allies Russia and China are permanent, veto-wielding members, the move is an escalation in a diplomatic standoff between Iran and Western powers, and Iran warned on Monday it would retaliate if the resolution passed.The text, proposed by the United States, Britain, France and Germany, passed with 23 votes in favour, three against and eight abstentions, diplomats at the closed-door International Atomic Energy Agency meeting said. The countries that opposed were Russia, China and Niger, they said."(The board) requests the (IAEA) Director General to report this resolution and the previously adopted resolutions ... to all Members of the Agency and to the Security Council and the General Assembly of the United Nations, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the IAEA Statute," the text read.While the finding of non-compliance predates the war between the United States and Iran and concerns Iran's failure to explain uranium traces found at undeclared sites that the agency spent years investigating, there is now another standoff over IAEA access to the sites bombed by Israel and the United States.

sources.headline: IAEA board passes resolution reporting Iran to UN Security Council

brief_bullets: The 35-nation board of governors of the International Atomic Energy Agency has passed a resolution reporting Iran to the United Nations Security Council for the first time in two decades due to serious breaches of its non-proliferation obligations. The measure, spearheaded by the United States, Britain, France, and Germany during a closed-door meeting in Vienna, secured 23 votes in favour, with opposition from Russia, China, and Niger, alongside eight abstentions. This escalation follows a prior finding of non-compliance concerning unexplained uranium traces at undeclared sites, compounded by ongoing disputes over IAEA access to nuclear facilities previously bombed by Israel and the United States. Although concrete punitive measures by the Security Council remain unlikely given the veto power held by Russian and Chinese allies, the formal referral significantly deepens the diplomatic standoff between Tehran and Western powers, prompting threats of retaliatory economic and military measures from Iranian officials.
why_it_matters_bullets: This formal UN referral marks a critical turning point in international non-proliferation diplomacy, entrenching geopolitical polarization and heightening the risk of further regional military escalation. While procedural vetoes may shield Iran from immediate UN sanctions, the breakdown in oversight severely diminishes global visibility into Tehran's nuclear program at a time of active physical conflict.

primary_source.headline: Google picks Finland for its largest single investment in Europe
primary_source.content: The US tech giant said the package would fund three new data centres, expand an existing site and support energy projects to power growing demand for AI services. "This is Google's largest single investment in Europe and a testament to Finland's leadership in responsibly building AI infrastructure," the company said on Wednesday. "Google's decision is a clear testament to our strengths," Finland's Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said in a statement. As part of the deal, Google signed a 22-year contract with Finnish utility Fortum to buy up to 50% of the output from the Loviisa nuclear power plant. Earlier this week, TikTok announced a $1bn investment in Finland to build a new data centre in Kouvola, pointing to the country's "strong digital infrastructure, clean energy mix, robust data governance and skilled tech talent". Finland has emerged as an attractive location for data centres because of its cool climate, plentiful low-carbon electricity and relatively uncongested power grid. The colder temperatures can reduce the energy needed to cool facilities packed with computer servers.

primary_source.headline: Apple CEO John Ternus says the best AI device is still the iPhone
primary_source.content: Apple’s new CEO John Ternus used the opening of the company’s Surprise and Shine event Wednesday to make its AI strategy clear: the iPhone is already the best AI device out there, and Apple cares more about data privacy than its rivals. The comments come as Ternus takes the reins at Apple from Tim Cook, who is now executive chairman, and offer a clear picture of how the company plans to compete in the AI era. Instead of building new hardware for AI, Apple wants to make the iPhone the central way consumers interact with the new technology. During his introduction at the Cupertino event, Ternus described the ideal AI device, or “intelligent personal hub,” as he called it. He said such a hub would have a broad understanding of a user’s personal context, always be with them, and have both a powerful processor capable of running AI models on-device and an internet connection to access models in the cloud. The device would also have a large display, high-quality cameras and microphones so it could see and hear the world around it, along with long battery life, Ternus continued. Plus, “you’d want it to be super easy to use without a big learning curve. And finally, you’d want it to work seamlessly with your other devices, apps, and services, so it feels like one integrated experience,” he said. “In other words, you would arrive at something remarkably familiar, because there’s no product in the world better designed to be your intelligent personal hub than iPhone,” Ternus said.

primary_source.headline: Apple launches iPhone 18 Pro with upgraded camera
primary_source.content: Apple launched its latest Pro phones, the iPhone 18 Pro and the iPhone 18 Pro Max, today at its fall “Surprise and Shine” iPhone event. While the design of the phones remains the same as the earlier model, the upgraded cameras are the highlight of the new devices. The new Pro series camera features a 48-megapixel camera with variable aperture, made with six thin blades. This system will likely improve low-light photography quality and speed. There are also new pro controls in the camera software, including white balance and histogram. The new Pro devices also have a smaller dynamic range island on the front of the device, which now allows you to track three live activities instead of two. Both phones are powered by Apple’s latest A20 Pro silicon and feature a newly designed vapor chamber for improved cooling. The company has also improved the battery with a better design. Apple also said the iPhone 18 Pro supports video playback of 36 hours, and the 18 Pro Max has 45 hours of playback capacity. The company showed off the new Siri AI with contextual on-screen intelligence. It said the new Siri AI will support English in beta at launch with the iOS 27 rollout this month, with French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish support coming in October. The new devices will also get the iPhone handoff feature with iOS 27 that allows you to use two iPhones with one eSIM and switch back and forth between them.

primary_source.headline: Bhadra water reaches Gonur Lake, farmers rejoice
primary_source.content: Chitradurga: Water released from the Bhadra reservoir towards the Chitradurga Branch Canal (CBC) as part of the Upper Bhadra Project reached Gonur Lake in the taluk around 3 pm on Wednesday. Farmers and residents welcomed the water, which they described as a lifeline, by performing Ganga pooja.Despite several hurdles and confusion surrounding the project, officials of Visvesvaraya Jala Nigam Limited (VJNL) succeeded in bringing the water to the designated&nbsp;164-km point.Water flowed for 114 km through the Chitradurga Branch Canal, which branches off to the left at the Ajjampura ‘Y’ junction in Tarikere taluk of Chikkamagaluru district. Including the 50-km stretch from the reservoir to the ‘Y’ junction, the trial flow covered a total distance of 164 km.Bhadra water reaches drought-prone ‘Kote Nadu’At Tarikere, local farmers had initially blocked the flow, insisting that water be released to their lakes before allowing it to proceed further. Similar hurdles were reported in parts of Hosadurga taluk. The issues were resolved amicably and the water was allowed to flow ahead.The water reached the drought-hit plains through Sanehalli in Hosadurga taluk on Tuesday. It entered Hiriyur taluk through Gaunahalli later that night and reached Kyadigere in Chitradurga taluk from Aymangala in Hiriyur taluk by Wednesday afternoon. From there, the water flowed through the canal constructed over Gonur hill before reaching the lake.Farmers expressed joy at seeing water flowing through the canal despite the severe drought conditions. Women farmers performed Ganga pooja on the banks of the canal, while several people offered flowers, leaves and betel nuts to the water. Many were visibly emotional as they watched the water descend from the hill towards the lake.“I never thought we would see Bhadra water in our lifetime. We had lost faith in the assurances of politicians. Seeing the water flowing now brings tears to my eyes,” said farmer Mahantesh.Celebration todayIn view of the Bhadra water reaching the district, the District Irrigation Struggle Committee has organised a welcome ceremony near Gonur at 10.30 am on September 10.The programme will be chaired by committee president and former MP P Kodandaramaiah. Seers, elected representatives and leaders of various organisations are expected to participate.Lake overflows within two hoursAs Gonur Lake was already full, it began overflowing within two hours. The water then reached Dyamavvanahalli in the taluk.Along the same stretch, seven to eight more lakes, up to Rani Lake in Challakere taluk, are expected to be filled.“Currently, around 700 cusecs of water is being released daily. More than 100 lakes, including 20 lakes in Tarikere taluk, are expected to be filled,” officials said.Water flows towards Gonur Lake.H Ravishankar, Chief Engineer VJNLThe initial trial flow has been successful. Going forward the aim is to complete the Gonur aqueduct works and divert water towards Challakere Molakalmuru Jagalur and Pavagada taluks.

Santosh Jigalikoppa, Haveri: Left alone, I become dung; touched, I become manure; burnt, I become sacred ash; placed without being touched, I become top dressing. O human, whom do you serve?”... These lines from poet S G Narasimhachar’s verse aptly underscore the value and varied uses of cow dung.As preparations for Ganesh festival celebrations gain momentum across the district, clay idols have entered markets, while some plaster of Paris (POP) idols are also being sold despite the ban.With fewer artisans making eco-friendly idols, young farmer Yallappa Dodmani from Kurubara Mallur village in Savanur taluk is making attractive idols from cow dung. His three-year-old initiative has now generated growing demand.Dodmani has practised organic farming for years using cow dung and urine and has received the Best Organic Farmer award at the Dharwad Agricultural University’s Krishi Mela. Keen to try something new alongside farming, he learned idol-making at training camps organised by Kanheri Mutt.Limited edition idolsAfter training, he began making idols using cow dung in his village. He made only 11 idols in the first year, distributing them locally. This year, he has made 40. Customers from Haveri, Ranebennur, Bengaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad and Davanagere districts are placing advance orders.Villagers who once wondered how Ganesha could be made from dung are now appreciating his work. Demand rises every year, but farming leaves him little time, so he makes only a limited number during his free hours. His wife, Nayana, assists him.Eco-friendly clay idols find takers ahead of Ganesh Chaturthi

"I pursue farming without chemicals and make these idols the same way. I use Panchagavya to prepare idols. These are eco-friendly, organic Ganesha idols," Dodmani said.Only two types of water colours are applied. Unlike heavier clay and POP idols, dung idols are lightweight. As dung contains little adhesive, he can make only three or four idols a day.Dodmani dries cow dung cakes in the sun for two months, mills them into powder, then mixes the powder with adhesive before shaping idols. He hopes others will make such idols and says he is ready to provide training.Yallappa Dodmani, Cow dung idol makerGanesha idols of various designs ranging from those installed at homes to those placed in public spaces can be made from cow dung. I am currently making idols for homes and am trying to develop one suitable for public installations.Ganesha idol sales gain momentum Demand for Ganesha idols to be installed during the festival has surged with many sellers taking advance bookings from customers for their preferred designs. Several artisan families have worked day and night to prepare the idols which are now stocked at shops and stalls across Haveri including near the Veerabhadreshwar Temple Ijarilakmapur Nagendranamatti Basaveshwaranagar and M G Road. Idols in various designs and sizes are also available for sale across Ranebennur Hangal Hirekerur Shiggaon Savanur Rattihalli and Byadagi taluks. The idols range from two to six feet in height.

primary_source.headline: MHA panel reviews Bezbaruah Committee reforms after Manipuri musician's death in Delhi
primary_source.content: New Delhi: In the wake of the murder of a Manipuri musician in Delhi, the Monitoring Committee on Northeast issues of the Union Ministry of Home Affairs, in a meeting on Tuesday, discussed key reforms, including recommendations of the Bezbaruah Committee for the amendments of Indian Penal Code that have not been taken up in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. The meeting had in attendance the Joint Secretary of the MHA’s North East Division, with representatives from various states and concerned government departments and agencies, including the officials from Delhi Police, DoNER and NCERT, besides MHA officials. Manipuri musician beaten to death for objecting to shouting, drinking outside his Delhi flatJoram Maivio, special invitee to the Monitoring Committee, who has also been a member of the Bezbaruah Committee, says that as per the recommendations of the Bezbaruah Committee, it was decided that there will be amendments to sections 153 (C) and 509 (A) of the Indian Penal Code. “The recommendations of the Bezbaruah Committee for the amendments of IPC which was to be taken up in the comprehensive amendments in the BNS was not taken up,” he said, adding that the issue was taken up in the meeting.  Other reforms, such as the need for the strictest possible action, along with concrete measures to prevent such incidents, appointment of Nodal Officers in metropolitan cities, and inclusion of North East history and culture in school curricula, among other measures, were discussed. Delhi lynching ends peace-loving Vikram's musical journey, reignites safety concern for Northeast residentsThe Monitoring Committee was formed after a Supreme Court directive in the Karma Dorjee PIL, which had also taken into account racial discrimination of other cases like the murder of student Nido Tania. The committee is mandated to oversee the recommendations of the Bezbaruah Committee, and must meet every three months, but attendees said that at least three chairpersons have changed and yet several recommendations are yet to be implemented.  The Bezbaruah Committee was formed after the murder of 19-year-old Tania under the chairmanship of retired IAS officer MP Bezbaruah. Some of the recommendations include a strict new anti-discrimination law, fast-track trials with investigations to be completed within 60 days and court trials within 90 days, strengthening the Special Police Unit for Northeast Region (SPUNER) and introducing aspects of Northeast Indian history, culture, and traditions into school curricula across India. Some of these were taken up during Tuesday’s meeting.

Rather than advocating extreme digital detoxes, she suggests simple “attention audits” and pockets of undivided attention, such as screen-free meals, phone-free conversations, walks without headphones and watching films without scrolling. stories.primary_headline: Dry spell hits inflows in rivers across Belagavi district

primary_source.headline: Dry spell hits inflows in rivers across Belagavi district
primary_source.content: Belagavi: A dry spell lasting nearly a fortnight has begun affecting water inflow into rivers across Belagavi district. The Malaprabha has recorded no inflow due to the lack of rainfall in its catchment areas in the Western Ghats region of Khanapur taluk, while inflow into the Ghataprabha has been declining for over a week. The Krishna, too, has witnessed a fall in inflow and was flowing below its average level on Wednesday.The Ghataprabha has recorded a steady decline in inflow. The Hidkal Dam received 1,657 cusecs of water on Wednesday. The dam has a maximum storage capacity of 51 TMC, including 48.980 TMC of live storage, and is currently filled to capacity. However, water discharge has been regulated in line with the inflow. The outflow from Hidkal Dam stood at 2,140 cusecs, including 1,500 cusecs released into the Ghataprabha Right Bank Canal (GRBC) and 450 cusecs into the Chikkodi Branch Canal (CBC).The Malaprabha has not received any inflow for over a week as the Western Ghats region of Khanapur taluk continues to experience a dry spell. Storage in the Malaprabha Dam stood at 21.818 TMC, of which 18.433 TMC was live storage.The dam was releasing 194 cusecs of water.Karnataka Neeravari Nigam Limited Assistant Executive Engineer at the Malaprabha Dam, Vivek Mudigoudar, said about 14 TMC of water would be required between September and May to meet the drinking water needs of Hubballi-Dharwad, Gadag and multi-village water supply schemes along the route, besides filling lakes to meet drinking water requirements.“Given the present storage, there is little flexibility to release water for irrigation. However, if the region receives more rain and storage increases by around 10 TMC, water could be released for irrigation,” he said.Mudigoudar added that evaporation losses were estimated at around 4 TMC.

primary_source.content: Chennai: The Tamil Nadu government has issued a formal order granting 'in-principle approval' for the construction of a new Legislative Assembly and Secretariat complex here at an estimated cost of Rs 1,200 crore.The modern facility will have a built-up area of 20 lakh square feet and will come up on 25.55 acres of land in Mylapore, according to a Government Order (GO) issued by the Public (Buildings) Department.Tamil Nadu CM Vijay says 'my body language of touching jaw in Assembly unintentional'The GO (Ms) No. 564, dated September 8, follows an announcement made by Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay on the floor of the Assembly on September 3 under Rule 110.According to the order, the government has identified specific land parcels in Mylapore Town for the project. The 25.55-acre area aggregates lands currently in the possession of the Tamil Nadu Housing Board, the Greater Chennai Corporation, and the Government Revenue Department.The Public Works Department (PWD) has been directed to submit a Detailed Project Report (DPR), along with the estimates, within three months.Further, the state government has ordered the constitution of three dedicated committees to oversee the project's design phase. These include a committee to call for an Expression of Interest (EoI) to finalise the architectural consultancy firm, alongside separate committees to finalise the preliminary and final building drawings and designs.Tamil Nadu Assembly witnesses uproar over CM Vijay's ED remarks, marshals evict DMK MLAsCM Vijay on September 3 anounced establishing a new Assembly-cum-Secretariat integrated complex, signalling the administration's decision to move out of the historic Fort St George.This modern integrated complex will house all state government departments and will be established at an estimated cost of Rs 1,200 crore on a built-up area of 20 lakh sq ft, he said.

stories.primary_headline: 13.53 lakh voters listed in draft electoral roll of Dharwad dist

primary_source.headline: 13.53 lakh voters listed in draft electoral roll of Dharwad dist
primary_source.content: Dharwad: As per the directions of the Election Commission of India (ECI), the Special Intensive Revision (SIR)-2026 of the electoral roll is underway in the district. The draft electoral roll was published on August 24, with 13.53 lakh voters included in it, said Additional Deputy Commissioner Geetha C D.Speaking to media persons here on Wednesday, she said that of the 16.21 lakh voters previously listed in the district, details of 13.53 lakh voters (83.48%), had been verified and included in the draft electoral roll.She informed that during the verification process under the SIR exercise, 2.68 lakh voters were identified under various categories, including absent, migrated, deceased and duplicate voters. Of these, 22,628 were from Navalgund, 19,078 from Kundgol, 32,007 from Dharwad, 47,034 from Hubballi-Dharwad East, 65,844 from Hubballi-Dharwad Central, 64,623 from Hubballi-Dharwad West and 16,801 from Kalghatgi, she informed.Karnataka SIR: Your name in the draft voter list doesn’t guarantee a place in the final rollThe district currently has 1,665 polling stations across its seven Assembly constituencies. Following approval from the Election Commission, steps have been taken to increase the number of polling stations to 1,707, she said.During the special campaign held on August 29 and 30, a total of 1,431 applications were received for various electoral services, including registration of new voters. These included 1,114 Form-6 applications, 18 Form-7 applications and 299 Form-8 applications.Voters can also apply for services such as inclusion of names, corrections and change of address through the Election Commission's Voters' Portal (voters.eci.gov.in) and the official ECI NET mobile application, she said.Eligible citizens have been advised to verify whether their names are included in the electoral roll. Those whose names are missing have been asked to submit applications within the prescribed period. Voters have also been urged to file claims and objections if they find any errors in the draft electoral roll, she said.Karnataka draft voter list out: 1.07 crore voters excluded. Here’s what to do if your name's missingShe informed that a total of 33,987 anomalies and 13,950 unmapped voters have been identified in the district and notices have been prepared in connection with these cases. A total of 47,939 notices were generated, of which 32,296 have been distributed, while distribution of the remaining 15,643 notices is pending. Hearings have been conducted in 2,587 cases, while the scheduled hearing date has passed in 2,657 cases, she added.The officer said that Electoral Registration Officers (EROs), Assistant Electoral Registration Officers (AEROs), Booth Level Officers (BLOs) and staff from various departments are working in coordination for the revision exercise. Officials from various departments have also been assigned additional responsibilities.
